# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The model implementation is not supplied; diagnosis uses a SASRec-compatible view. `view.model` is the actual trained module, while `view.item_emb`, `log2feats(sequence)` and `predict_score(features, items)` expose embeddings, sequence features and scores. For history interventions, histories are truncated, left-padded, encoded into `B × L × H` features, and read from the final position. Margin probes use features at every valid position.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` reads training histories, optional timestamps, and public item titles/descriptions. `run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)` switches the actual module to evaluation mode, disables gradients, and restores its previous mode afterward. Loader batches contain `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` tensors of shape `B × L`; padding positions are excluded.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding alignment:** Samples up to 2,048 nonpadding item embeddings and returns `(1 + mean pairwise cosine)/2`. Values near 1 indicate directional alignment; approximately 0.5 indicates orthogonality. Alignment alone cannot establish collapse or recommendation diversity.
- **Positive–negative separation:** Across at most ten batches, measures positive-minus-sampled-negative scores: mean, 10th percentile, fraction below zero, and fraction below 0.5. Larger margins and fewer ranking reversals generally indicate stronger sampled separation, but margin magnitudes depend on score scale and negative sampling.
- **History sensitivity:** Measures top-10 disruption, displacement of the original top item, and change in the original top-versus-runner-up score gap. Greater sensitivity is not inherently better or worse.

# Perturbation & Tests

With supplied remaining budget, up to 32 training users undergo compact history deletions and shuffles, including a shuffle preserving the last item. Deletion groups distinguish recent positions and recurrence identified through duplicate IDs or title/description TF-IDF similarity. Five exactly matched control draws estimate excess sensitivity; infeasible matches are skipped.

Each user retains a fixed full-catalog candidate set excluding all original training items. Repeat scoring checks determinism; positive score rescaling checks ranking invariance. Summaries aggregate by user and prefix length, with descriptive bootstrap intervals.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

The returned object contains `metrics` and `metric_definitions`. Metrics include embedding alignment, four margin statistics, unavailable category breakdowns, nested perturbation records/summaries/coverage, and runtime/allocation reporting.

Perturbations require shared-budget information; interrupted users contribute no partial results. These probes measure training-data behavior, not held-out accuracy or causal preferences. Unavailable metadata and simulator traits are never inferred. Four-dataset aggregation and checkpoint selection remain external responsibilities.
